The pod controls are sound as far as they go — I reproduced both and added a stronger one — but neither shows a GitHub-hosted runner completing a job with registry-1.docker.io, mirror.gcr.io and proxy.golang.org unreachable, which is the claim acceptance 1 makes about CI. failures.criterion: Acceptance 1 — "Each fetch named in that catalog comes from a source this repository controls or pins", as enforced by .github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh, the gate this change adds
failures.evidence: The gate passes a Dockerfile that builds FROM a third-party image, silently, when the image is named through an ARG default. scan_dockerfile (.github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh:641-650) skips any FROM holding a variable the Dockerfile declares as an ARG, without reading that ARG's default value; Docker builds FROM the default when no --build-arg overrides it, so the default is the image the build fetches. Observed at a13294ef: adding `ARG SNEAKY_BASE=docker.io/library/debian:trixie-slim` and `FROM ${SNEAKY_BASE}` to packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile left `bash .github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh` at exit 0, its summary line dropping from 34 references to 33 with no refusal; the mutation was reverted and the working copy was clean afterwards. This is the shape the FROM lines had before this change (`ARG BUN_VERSION=1.4.4` with `FROM oven/bun:${BUN_VERSION}`), so it is the shape a return to Docker Hub takes, and the gate is the only thing standing against it. Red test: .github/scripts/check-ci-images.test.sh, case `a FROM on an ARG whose default is a third-party image`, committed at 92714a7244ab. `bash .github/scripts/check-ci-images.test.sh` prints `Results: 65 passed, 2 failed` and exits 1 (it printed `65 passed, 0 failed` before the case). The fix is to substitute a declared ARG's default into the FROM and read the result as a reference like any other.

failures.criterion: Acceptance 1 — the gate's exception list, whose header states that each entry carries exactly one ground and that a ground which holds nothing is a ground nobody reads again
failures.evidence: EXCEPTIONS gives packages/envoy/scripts/corpus-copy.sh the ground `a CI job runs it, and it fetches nothing` (.github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh:223). Both halves are false. No CI job runs it: `grep -rIn corpus-copy` over the tree finds it only in the gate itself, packages/envoy/scripts/README.md, cmd/dispatch/README.md, CHANGELOG.md, search_bench_test.go's comment and three sibling scripts' error messages, and no .github/workflows file names it; it also refuses to start without DISPATCH_BACKUP_BUCKET and requires `aws`, `psql` and `pg_restore`. And it does fetch: line 53 is `docker run -d --name "$container" ... mirror.gcr.io/pgvector/pgvector@sha256:2358fcba...`. Its correct ground is `no CI job runs it`, the one the sibling developer scripts carry. (By contrast the two other FETCHES_NOTHING entries hold: ci.yaml's `test` job runs scripts/dev-postgres.test.sh, which puts a fake `docker` on PATH before running dev-postgres.sh, and check-bun-version.test.sh writes its references into fixture files under a temporary directory.) No red test pins this: the gate cannot tell which files CI runs, which is why the ground is written by hand and has to be right.

failures.criterion: INFRA-520 READY risk, delivered here: "docs-pages.yaml repeats the 14 steps of ci.yaml's docs job ... Make one source of the steps ... so the two cannot drift" — the consolidated path main actually runs
failures.evidence: The shared build is proven for ci.yaml's caller (its docs job calls docs-site.yaml on every pull request), but main's caller runs two steps no pull request can reach: docs-site.yaml's `actions/upload-pages-artifact` step, gated on `inputs.upload-pages-artifact`, and docs-pages.yaml's `deploy` job, which looks the `github-pages` artifact up in the run. docs-pages.yaml's `on:` is `push: branches: [main]` alone (no workflow_dispatch, no pull_request), so the first execution of the artifact crossing the called-workflow boundary is after the merge, and a failure there stops the documentation site from updating with no pull request able to show it. The missing surface, and the cheapest one that does not publish a branch build to the live site: add `workflow_dispatch:` to docs-pages.yaml and gate its `deploy` job on `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, then dispatch the workflow on legion/INFRA-567 and quote the run showing `build` uploading the `github-pages` artifact and `deploy` skipped. No red test pins this: it is a run that has not happened.

A pull request that adds a row races its own gate. mirror-images.yaml and ci.yaml's lint job start together on a pull_request event, and check 7 fails with `is not in the package: a manifest HEAD answered 404` until crane has copied the row. The gate's message says the usual remedy is to merge the row and let the mirror run, but on the pull request that adds it the two run concurrently, so a slow crane install turns lint red and the fix is a re-run — the thing acceptance 2 counts. Making lint's gate skip check 7 for a row the pull request adds, or ordering the two, would remove it.

Check 7 puts ghcr.io's availability on the lint job's critical path (the implementer records this as its own open question 3). One anonymous token request plus one manifest HEAD per row, 13 requests, with no retry and no cache.

proof.criterion: R2 — a Go command in CI survives a failure of proxy.golang.org
proof.surface: The Go toolchain CI runs (go1.27.1) with GOPROXY set to the value every workflow and the three Dockerfile Go stages now carry, a fresh module cache, and the proxy pointed at a dead address
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && GOMODCACHE=<fresh> GOFLAGS= GOWORK=off GOPROXY='http://127.0.0.1:1|direct' GOSUMDB='sum.golang.org http://127.0.0.1:1' go mod download github.com/jackc/pgx/v5
proof.observed: exit 0, 4.4 MB written to the fresh cache (v5.11.0.info, .mod, .zip, .ziphash). The module came through `direct` with both the proxy and the checksum database unreachable, which is the stronger reading: go.sum already holds the hash, so no checksum-database lookup is on the path. All five workflow files that run go set `GOPROXY: https://proxy.golang.org|direct` at workflow level and no job or step overrides it; worker.Dockerfile, packages/envoy/docker/Dockerfile and heldportwrapper/Dockerfile each set the same value as ENV.
proof.negativeControl: The same command with today's separator, GOPROXY='http://127.0.0.1:1,direct' -> exit 1, `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused`: a comma falls through only after a 404 or a 410, which is why a mid-stream reset turned the Go lane red.
